items.title: Russia’s crude oil production fell again in September, averaging 8.643 million barrels per day, according to OPEC data. That was 38,000 bpd below August, which itself was down 174,000 bpd from July. September output stood 1.306 million bpd below Russia’s OPEC+ quota. Russian refineries also remained under pressure from Ukrainian strikes, with crude processing averaging below 4 million bpd compared with a pre-campaign seasonal norm of 5.4 to 5.5 million bpd. #Russia

Satellite imagery from October 12 reportedly showed drones already being unloaded at the site. The source said the construction pattern closely resembled the Tsymbulova facility. #Russia

items.title: Russian forces are reinforcing the Huliaipole axis as Moscow seeks to occupy the left-bank part of Zaporizhzhia Oblast, a Ukrainian Defense Forces source told Interfax-Ukraine. Russian forces were reportedly tasked with advancing 30 km by the end of October. The same source put Russia’s force advantage at 4:1 across the axis and up to 7:1 in the most threatened sectors. Three Rubicon drone units were rotating through the area, while infiltration remained Russia’s main tactic and armored vehicle use was minimal. #Ukraine

items.title: RT by @DefMon3: In Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East, we are seeing early drone warfare. I would equate this to where Ukraine and Russia were in 2023. The diffusion of drone technology and tactics will increase, particularly whenever the Russo-Ukraine war ends. I doubt that we are prepared.
items.summary:
In Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East, we are seeing early drone warfare. I would equate this to where Ukraine and Russia were in 2023. The diffusion of drone technology and tactics will increase, particularly whenever the Russo-Ukraine war ends. I doubt that we are prepared.
Ryan O'Leary (@RyanO_ChosenCoy)
One thing that is becoming more common is “PMC” type and drone companies hiring foreigners who did drones in Ukraine for work. The main problem with that, is that anyone can learn to fly a drone in 14-21 days. Give them 6 weeks and they’ll be hitting targets. What they don’t learn in-depth typically is the tactics behind drones (especially for the 6 monthers) or get a good grasp on signals/frequency and all the overly nerdy shit involved in that realm.
Not understanding frequencies and drone tactics in general will create a lot of scenarios such as this as outside of the Ukrainian war, front areas are not saturated with signals and hundreds of drones flying around so it’s much more easy to pinpoint launch positions and also signal locations.
“One of the sources who works for Congo's government said that Rwandan forces backing the M23 rebels may have surprised them by tracking a drone ​used for surveillance operations to their location.”
reuters.com/world/africa/eri…

items.title: RT by @COUPSURE: Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia. As of now, sadly, twelve people have been confirmed killed, including three children. My condolences to all their families and loved ones. Another fourteen people have been injured, and two of them are in critical condition – the doctors are fighting to save their lives. The status of twelve more people who may have been there is still being verified. All emergency services are at the scene, and search-and-rescue operations are underway. Overnight, thirteen of our regions came under attack. Residential buildings, infrastructure, and railway facilities have been damaged. Last night confirmed once again that in Russia, they take any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed. Russia must understand that it needs to stop the war, and for that to happen, Russia must feel its losses. Right now, it is our long-range capabilities that are ensuring this. And we will respond to Russian strikes. I thank everyone who is helping.
